setup.data: 948 synthetic social-pressure situations (target ~950-1000) generated by GPT-4o-mini: 8 context types x 8 pressure mechanisms (authority appeal, emotional manipulation, social consequences, flattery, conflict risk, group conformity, reciprocity, moral reframing) x ~20 variants; each 2-4 sentences, pressure to agree with or accommodate the user. These are social/interpersonal dilemmas (praise for flawed work, a loan request), NOT factual questions with a gold answer. Each situation x 4 system-prompt personas (PA, SI, DCA, neutral baseline) = 3,792 prompts for activations; an anti-sycophancy persona is added for behavioural tests (5,000 responses = 1,000 situations x 5; the per-mechanism n in Figure 29 sums to 1,000, so the behavioural set is the full 1,000 while activations use 948; Figure 1 legend shows n=947 per cluster). Train/test split 80/20 by situation ID (758/189 situations). Persona-free control: 80 hand-authored scenarios (20 per class) where the mode is induced by a different trigger per mode, no persona prompt.
setup.models_and_sizes: Gemma-2-9B-it only (TransformerLens). Judges: GPT-4o-mini and Claude Sonnet 4.6; sentence-transformer for output embeddings; DeBERTa-xlarge-MNLI BERTScore.
setup.layers_positions: Residual stream blocks.{l}.hook_resid_post at layers 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34, last prompt token only. L18 = primary geometry layer, L22 = primary causal layer. Logit lens over all layers (shown up to L40). Head analyses: 16 heads x 6 layers = 96 heads. Necessity uses next-token KL at the last token.
setup.baselines: Neutral-persona baseline run per situation (deviation vectors subtract it); random k orthonormal directions and full-layer zeroing as floor/ceiling for necessity; mean-ablation vs zero-ablation for heads; anti-sycophancy persona as behavioural lower bound; text-only LLM-judge 5-way classification as the output-space comparison.
setup.controls: Paired design (same situation under all personas); split by situation ID; ICA vs PCA basis check; complement-subspace probe after removing top-10 directions; second judge (kappa 0.67, r 0.95); persona-free scenarios with a 2000-permutation null; persona->persona-free transfer with and without per-regime z-scoring. Missing: no second model, no seeds/CIs on most numbers, no steering, no per-item correctness labels, no matching across items on any confidence variable.

figures.what_is_plotted: Summary of the three hypothesised modes: mechanism, HEXACO trait profile, output signature, predicted geometry, trigger mechanism.
figures.takeaway: Modes are defined a priori; predicted geometry: PA intermediate, SI most distant from DCA, DCA closest to baseline; triggers: PA group pressure/warmth, SI flattery/status, DCA conflict risk/moral reframing.
figures.numbers: none

figures.what_is_plotted: 2D PCA of L18 activations, left = ground-truth labels (4 classes), right = K-means assignment (k=4).
figures.takeaway: Four very tight, widely separated blobs; K-means recovers them perfectly.
figures.numbers: ARI train = test = 1.000, NMI 1.000; n=947 per cluster (legend). In 2D: SI top centre, PA and DCA adjacent (PA-DCA gap ~1/3 of PA-SI gap), baseline far left at roughly equal 2D distance from all three modes (checked at 300 dpi; approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Legend is readable at 300 dpi. 'DCA closest to PA' and 'SI set apart' hold in the plot. 'Baseline closest to DCA' is not visible in these two PCs (baseline is about equidistant); it rests on the PCA-50 nearest-neighbour numbers in Table 3. n=947 per cluster vs 948 situations in the text.

figures.what_is_plotted: F3 summary per mode: sufficiency (k=8), necessity ceiling (L22, PCA), complement recall (L18), judge 5-way accuracy.
figures.takeaway: SI is compact and easy to detect in text; DCA distributed and hard to detect; necessity is tiny for all modes.
figures.numbers: PA/SI/DCA: sufficiency 0.86/0.98/0.40; necessity 0.063/0.008/0.012; complement recall 0.41/0.29/0.31; judge accuracy 48.6%/72.0%/18.7%.
figures.mismatch_note: Caption says DCA is 'most distributed', but its complement recall at L18 (0.31) is nearly as low as SI (0.29) and lower than PA (0.41). The 'necessity ceiling (L22)' row is not DCA's ceiling (DCA peaks at L26, 0.044, Table 9) and not SI's under ICA (0.068, Table 17).

figures.what_is_plotted: L18 principal angles between the 50-dim deviation subspaces of PA-SI, PA-DCA, SI-DCA: angle vs sorted PC dimension (left), count of dimensions per angle bracket (center), share of deviation variance per bracket (right).

figures.what_is_plotted: Selected L22 head zero-ablation KL per mode and specificity multipliers.

figures.mismatch_note: Headers render cleanly in the page image (Head, PA KL, SI KL, DCA KL, PAx, SIx, DCAx); the garbling is only in paper.txt extraction. Raw KL values are 0.001-0.018 nats, very small. Caption says H10/H11 'fire comparably across all three modes', but their zero-ablation KL is PA ~2x SI (0.005 vs 0.002; 0.011 vs 0.007), matching the PA-dominant bars in Figures 20 and 22.

figures.what_is_plotted: Pairwise joint ablation additivity for PA head pairs.

figures.what_is_plotted: Simultaneous ablation of TOP-6 and TOP-10 heads per mode.
figures.takeaway: TOP-6 strongly subadditive (compensation); even TOP-10 is <5% of full-layer effect.
figures.mismatch_note: Internally odd: TOP-6 PA joint KL (0.00567) is about 6x smaller than the joint KL of the pair L22H9+L22H3 (0.032, Table 14), both of which are top PA-selective heads and presumably in TOP-6 (membership is never listed). Ablating more heads giving much less disruption is not explained; adding 4 heads (TOP-10) then raises joint KL 12x. Treat the 'compensation' reading as unverified. '% full-layer' is relative to zeroing the whole layer, a very large denominator.

key_results.claim: Modes are near-indistinguishable in text but perfectly linearly separable inside.
key_results.quote: Although the modes produce highly similar outputs, with a text-only classifier achieving just 57.8% accuracy, their internal representations are perfectly linearly separable from layer 14 onward.

key_results.claim: Geometry peaks before output commitment: logit lens is silent until ~L23.
key_results.quote: despite being internally separable by layer 18, the three modes produce nearly identical token distributions until approximately layer 23.

key_results.claim: Mode subspaces are sufficient when injected but not necessary when ablated (<7%).
key_results.quote: removing the same directions from sycophantic forward passes produces minimal behavioral disruption, with ICA and PCA variants both yielding less than 7% change

key_results.claim: Even the most specialised head circuit carries a tiny share of the layer's effect.
key_results.quote: Ablating all of PA's highest-priority heads together disrupts less than 5% of the layer's causal effect

key_results.claim: Only PA has selective heads; none for SI or DCA.
key_results.quote: 26 of 96 attention heads across 6 layers are PA-selective (>1.5× more disruption for PA when ablated); 0 SI-selective and 0 DCA-selective

key_results.claim: Top heads compensate for each other (redundancy / self-repair).
key_results.quote: the six priority heads compensate for each other almost entirely when all are ablated together

key_results.claim: Baseline sits inside DCA's region in activation space.
key_results.quote: The model's neutral baseline lands overwhelmingly in DCA's representational region, 85% of its activation-space nearest neighbors are DCA modes.

key_results.claim: Pressure type modulates which subspace is engaged (F6, stated qualitatively; no numbers reported).
key_results.quote: Conversely, mechanisms that induce a mode weakly often bypass its identifiable subspace.
Linear probes trained on persona-free layer-18 activations separate the modes with 96.7% accuracy (5-fold CV)

key_results.claim: Probe transfer across regimes fails raw and recovers only after offset removal; centroid directions weakly aligned.
key_results.quote: Class-centroid directions in the persona and persona-free regimes are positively but weakly aligned (cosine 0.08-0.12)

methods.name: Paired deviation vectors (mode activation minus same-item baseline activation)
methods.what_it_measures: The condition-induced shift with item content cancelled.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Preprocessing for all fates; for us: pressure-run minus neutral-run activation per item, split by flipped vs resisted.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Inject mean deviation (sufficiency) or project it out (necessity).
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Two forward passes per item; cheap at 9B.

methods.name: Principal angles between deviation subspaces, by layer, with shared-dimension count (cos > 0.9) and variance-weighted angle brackets
methods.what_it_measures: How much two conditions' shift subspaces overlap, layer by layer, robust to within-subspace rotation.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: H1 directly (pushback vs competing-answer subspaces); a flipped-vs-resisted version could show where routing splits (fates 3/4).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Ablate shared vs condition-specific dimensions separately and compare behaviour.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Hundreds of items per condition; 50-dim PCA per condition per layer; trivial compute.

methods.name: Normalised subspace necessity = (KL_ablate - KL_random)/(KL_full - KL_random) plus sufficiency by injection
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a subspace is causally needed vs just sufficient, normalised against random directions and full-layer zeroing.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Fate 2 bypass (decodable, injection works or not, ablation does nothing) vs fate 3 not routed; but low necessity can also be redundancy (see pitfalls).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Joint ablation across layers to rule out redundancy before calling bypass.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: 3 extra forward passes per item per layer per k.

methods.name: Complement-subspace probe (remove top-k directions, re-probe)
methods.what_it_measures: How much decodable information lies outside the identified subspace.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Fate 5 transformed vs 6 erased: if the correct-answer signal is gone from the main direction but recoverable in the complement, it moved rather than vanished.

methods.name: Logit-lens KL from baseline per layer and 'commitment layer' (first layer KL > 0.1)
methods.what_it_measures: When the condition's next-token prediction diverges.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Locates the override point (fate 4) when compared with the layer where the correct-answer probe stays high.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Patch at layers just before commitment.

methods.name: Head zero- vs mean-ablation specificity, cross-condition selectivity, pairwise and group additivity
methods.what_it_measures: Which heads carry condition-specific signal and whether heads are synergistic or redundant.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Override heads (fate 4) that read the user's claim; additivity shows hydra-style backup that would masquerade as bypass.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Targeted head ablation/steering as a Stage B fix.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: 96 heads x items x 3 ablation types; moderate at 9B.

methods.name: Cross-regime probe transfer with per-regime z-scoring (offset removal)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a probe trained in one regime reads the same variable in another, after removing a constant translation.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: H3 and fate 5: a probe trained on normal behaviour may fail on pressured runs only because of an offset; z-score first, then Procrustes, before calling it transformed.

controls_worth_copying: Random-k-directions floor and full-layer-zeroing ceiling for every subspace ablation (normalised necessity).
Zero-ablation vs mean-ablation of heads; pairwise and group joint ablation to detect redundancy before concluding a component is unused.
ICA vs PCA basis check for subspace results.
Split by item ID so the same item never appears in train and test.
Second, architecturally different judge with kappa and correlation reported.
Per-regime z-scoring before cross-condition probe transfer, reported alongside raw transfer.
Label-permutation null for small-n probe results.

pitfalls.pitfall: Modes are induced by different system prompts; last-token activations then differ mainly because the prompt text differs, so perfect separability is close to guaranteed and says little about computation.
pitfalls.quote: Persona conditioning is implemented entirely through the system prompt

pitfalls.pitfall: The authors themselves say separability may come from text regularities, not internal states.
pitfalls.quote: The linear separability we observe may reflect statistical and distributional regularities of the situation text rather than genuine motivational states.

pitfalls.pitfall: Persona-free control confounds mode with scenario content: each mode has its own trigger type and baseline is a neutral factual exchange; n = 80.
pitfalls.quote: baseline by a neutral, low-stakes, factual exchange in which honesty carries no social cost

pitfalls.pitfall: No factual ground truth: scenarios are social dilemmas, so 'sycophancy' is a judge score, and nothing tests whether a correct answer is decodable while the model yields.
pitfalls.quote: Each generated scenario is 2-4 sentences long and places the responder under social pressure to agree with or accommodate the user's position.

pitfalls.pitfall: Causal effects measured as next-token KL at the last prompt token only (first response token), with KL values of 0.002-0.018 nats for heads; not a behavioural outcome.
pitfalls.quote: record KLablate of next-token logits from the unablated run

pitfalls.pitfall: Low necessity is read as 'redundant representation', but no cross-layer joint ablation is done; low necessity could equally be bypass. For us: low ablation effect alone cannot separate bypass from redundancy.
pitfalls.quote: Thus, these directions summarize sycophancy modes but do not form necessary causal bottlenecks.

pitfalls.pitfall: Necessity is normalised by zeroing the whole layer, a huge ceiling, so '<7%' is small by construction and says little in absolute terms. KL_ablate is measured against the unablated mode run, so it measures how much the output is perturbed, not whether it moves toward the non-sycophantic baseline. For us: report absolute effects on the answer (flip rate, logit margin) and use 'patch in the neutral-run value' as the ceiling, not layer zeroing.
pitfalls.quote: To normalize, we compare this against ablating k random orthonormal directions and against zeroing the full layer output

pitfalls.pitfall: At the output layer the first-token distributions of mode and baseline nearly coincide (logit-lens KL 0.05-0.11 at L40, ~0 at L41 in Figure 7). All causal metrics are next-token KL at that token, so they track a quantity that barely differs between sycophantic and baseline runs; the judged multi-token behaviour is never tied to an intervention.
pitfalls.quote: Three phases: silent encoding (L1-L22, KL<0.06 despite perfect geometric separation at L18), rapid commitment (L23-L31), peak-and-collapse (L32L41)

pitfalls.pitfall: The redundancy story rests on TOP-6 subadditivity, but TOP-6 PA joint KL (0.0057) is below the joint KL of one PA head pair (0.032, Table 14); TOP-6 membership is not given. The compensation claim may be a bookkeeping artefact.
pitfalls.quote: TOP-6 is strongly subadditive (0.17–0.24): the six priority heads compensate for each other almost entirely when all are ablated together

pitfalls.pitfall: Sufficiency std is 2-6x the mean for PA and DCA, so per-item sufficiency is unreliable.
pitfalls.quote: None stated (our reading of Table 16: PA 0.858 +- 2.30, DCA 0.395 +- 2.32)

pitfalls.pitfall: F6 (pressure type changes the internal pathway) has no reported numbers; the cited Appendix J contains only head-ablation and subspace tables, no per-mechanism analysis.
pitfalls.quote: Full pressure-mechanism analyses and causal profiles are in Appendix J.

pitfalls.pitfall: A constant persona offset makes raw probe transfer fall to chance; a probe trained on one regime can fail on another for this reason alone.
pitfalls.quote: the presence/absence of the persona prompt induces a large constant offset in the residual stream

pitfalls.pitfall: Several caption/text mismatches (Fig 5 Mahalanobis vs cosine panel; Fig 19 'only PA-selective head' vs 26 heads; Fig 28 '100% shared' vs 37/50; n=1 pressure row in Figs 3 and 29; 13 context labels in Fig 34).

limitations_quote: The linear separability we observe may reflect statistical and distributional regularities of the situation text rather than genuine motivational states.
future_work_quote: the controllability implications are predictions from the representational geometry that we plan to validate with steering experiments in future work

bears_on_fates.how: Their mode subspaces are decodable (100%) and sufficient when injected, but ablation changes next-token output by <7% of a full-layer-zeroing ceiling: a decodable-but-not-necessary pattern. They call it redundancy (TOP-6 heads subadditive 0.17-0.24), without cross-layer joint ablation, and the TOP-6 numbers are internally odd (see pitfalls). Lessons: (1) our bypass test needs joint/multi-layer ablation or redundancy will look like bypass; (2) normalise against a meaningful ceiling (neutral-run patch) and measure the answer, not first-token KL, or 'small necessity' is uninformative.
bears_on_fates.strength: moderate (as a method caution), weak as evidence

bears_on_fates.how: Three-stage timing (geometry L18, causal L22/L26, logit commitment L23-33) shows where a pressure signal starts to act; a correct-answer probe tracked across the same layers could locate an override. They never measure a competing correct signal.

Cross-regime transfer fails raw and recovers to 0.817 only after z-scoring; centroid directions align at cosine 0.08-0.12. A probe failing across conditions can be an offset, not a re-encoding. Translate, then rotate (Procrustes), before calling it transformed.
Not addressed; no correct-answer variable exists in their data.

bears_on_group_angle: Close match in method, not in question. They run principal angles between per-condition deviation subspaces (50-dim PCA) at 6 layers, with shared-dimension counts (cos > 0.9) and variance-weighted angle brackets: a coarse layerwise subspace trajectory. Copy: the paired-deviation step, the rotation-robust shared-dim count, the variance-weighted brackets, and the layer sweep (divergence peaks at L18 and then PA-DCA re-converge to 37/50 shared dims by L34: subspaces split and re-merge across depth). What they do not do: Grassmannian paths or geodesic distances, flipped vs resisted contrasts, matching on prior confidence, Procrustes, token-path analysis, or a correct-answer subspace. Their L22H10 shifts attention toward the persona (system-prompt) tokens; it is only a loose analogue of our 'head that reads the user's claim' (it reads the instruction that sets the pressure, its ablation KL is ~0.005 nats, and it is redundant with L22H11). Their 'situation attention fraction' metric is the closer template: for us, attention fraction on the pushback turn, split by flipped vs resisted.
bears_on_H1_H2_H3: H1: indirect, weak support. In the main pipeline 'modes' are persona prompts, not pressures, so mode separability is not evidence for H1. Appendix N is the one place where pressure type alone is varied (vulnerable interlocutor vs status reward vs hostile threat, no persona): those states are 96.7-100% linearly separable, but n=80, each mode has its own scenario content, and separating different texts is near-trivial, so it shows decodability of the pressure context, not different fates. F6 (pressure type modulates subspace and head engagement) is stated without numbers. Behaviourally, pressure type matters only modestly (moral reframing 0.79-0.87 vs flattery 0.93-0.99 in Fig 3, no CIs), and the baseline varies too (0.25-0.40), so part of this is item difficulty. The shared dominant direction plus mode-specific mid-variance dimensions predicts a shared 'yield' axis plus pressure-specific components: a testable H1 prior. H2: not tested; no fixes, no DPO; they only predict that mode-targeted fixes should beat a single sycophancy direction. H3: partial support by analogy: a persona-trained mode probe transfers at chance raw and only 0.45-0.82 after z-scoring, so probes trained in one regime miss states in another. It is a mode-label probe, not a correctness probe.
overlap_with_our_plan: Stage A: none of the fate test. No factual items, no correct-answer probe, no flipped-vs-resisted split, no matching on confidence, no per-item fate assignment, no logit-margin control. What it does that overlaps with our group-angle toolkit: per-condition deviation subspaces, principal angles across layers, sufficiency/necessity with random and full-layer controls, head ablation specificity and additivity, logit-lens commitment layer, probe transfer with offset removal. Stage B: none (no fix, no DPO, no recheck; steering is future work). Left open: everything about knowledge-action divergence on factual items, the six fates, H2, and whether pressure types (pushback vs competing answer) differ in routing of a correct-answer signal. Scoop risk: low. Main risk is framing: 'sycophancy is not one thing; different pressures use different internal routes' is now claimed (F6, plus the pressure-only Appendix N control) on social scenarios with Gemma-2-9B, so our H1 must be framed as fates of a decodable correct answer, not as 'multiple sycophancy mechanisms'. Cite it.
architecture_location: Gemma-2-9B-it, last prompt token, residual stream. Mode geometry peaks L18; mode-subspace necessity peaks L22 (PA) and L26 (DCA); logit lens commits from L23, peaks L32-33, and collapses to ~0 by L41. Heads: L22H1 general (high zero- and mean-ablation KL); L22H10/H11 called a shared high-specificity hub (L22H10 shifts attention to persona tokens), though their ablation KL is PA ~2x and they are a redundant pair; L30H7 highest specificity (13-23x), invisible to attention metrics; PA synergistic trio L22H9, L22H3, L26H6; L26H12 big attention shift but causally inert. All head effects are 0.001-0.018 nats.
actionable_fix: None tested. Suggested: mode-specific contrastive steering vectors instead of one sycophancy direction; circuit-level intervention for PA, representation-level for SI/DCA; evaluate with internal measures, not only output judges. For us: their ablations (one subspace, or up to 10 heads, <5-7% of a full-layer-zeroing effect on first-token KL) are a warning that single-direction ablation may be weak, but they never measure behaviour after ablation, so they do not show that single-direction ablation fails as a fix. Stage B should measure flip rate directly.
reuse_verdict: Reuse methods, not conclusions. Copy the paired-deviation + layerwise principal-angle pipeline, the normalised necessity metric with random/full controls, the zero-vs-mean head ablation with additivity checks, and the z-score-before-transfer step. Do not cite its separability or F6 as evidence for H1: modes are system-prompt-induced, effects are tiny next-token KLs, and F6 has no numbers.
relevance_to_project: Medium. Not a scoop: it studies persona-induced social agreement with no correct answer, so it says nothing about the fate of decodable correct information. It is the closest worked example of our group-angle toolkit (subspace principal angles by layer, sufficiency vs necessity, head specificity) applied to sycophancy at an affordable size (Gemma-2-9B, the same model as our first fate run). It also gives two cautions we must design for: low ablation effect can be redundancy rather than bypass, and probe-transfer failure can be a constant offset rather than a transformation.
